svg.title: Azure Local: cloud control, local infrastructure
svg.desc: An infographic with three numbered sections. Section 1 is the Azure control plane, which handles management requests such as creating a virtual machine. A management arrow connects it to section 2, a local hyperconverged cluster. The two example physical nodes, 2A and 2B, each run VMs through Hyper-V and supply eligible local drives. Storage traffic connects both nodes to 2C, Storage Spaces Direct, which combines their drives into resilient shared storage. This shared storage is a logical pool across the nodes, not a separate external storage appliance. The local data plane carries workload application and storage traffic. Cluster coordination supports the failures covered by the design, while machines, switches, and storage remain at the site. Section 3 explains that control-plane health does not establish local workload health, and running workloads do not establish Azure management connection health. Arrows illustrate management and storage relationships, not a complete packet route.
svg.text: Azure Local: cloud control, local infrastructure
Read 1-3 top to bottom; within 2, read A-B-C. Example: two nodes.

g.text: Management requests, such as creating a virtual machine.
The same physical machines provide compute and storage.
Resilient shared storage from these nodes' drives.
Local data plane: workload application and storage traffic.
Cluster coordination supports the failures covered by the design.
Machines, switches, and storage remain at your site.
A healthy Azure control plane does not prove local workload health.
Running workloads do not prove a healthy Azure management connection.
